page: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs powered by the Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture operating at 3.0 GHz. Designed with a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the system integrates 96.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) alongside a bundled 1933 GB local SSD. It does not include dedicated GPU accelerators. Cache hierarchy comprises 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by hardware-accelerated AES cryptographic instructions.

Benchmark outcomes show that the 48 independent single-threaded cores scale parallel throughput effectively, registering in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core execution (85,051.53), Clang software compilation (39,975.0), and Redis SET operations (62.24 million operations per second). Conversely, single-core capabilities are comparatively modest, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1,117.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 8.92 GB/sec falling within the lower quartile. Memory throughput maintains mid-tier results across uncached 256 MB reads (176.14 GB/sec) and writes (76.83 GB/sec).

Cost efficiency is driven by the resource density of the Neoverse-N1 cores combined with bundled local scratch storage, delivering strong parallel capacity without the overhead of higher memory tiers. The architectural tradeoff centers on lower per-thread execution speeds and constrained per-core memory allocation. Consequently, the instance is well suited for highly parallelized workloads such as code compilation pipelines, Redis-backed in-memory caching, container orchestration, and multi-threaded web serving, but it is unsuited for memory-dense analytics or tasks bound to single-thread latency.
description: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v5 is an ARM64 compute instance featuring 48 dedicated physical cores on the Ampere Neoverse-N1 platform at 3.0 GHz, coupled with 96.0 GB of RAM and 1933 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Designed with a 2.0 GB per core ratio and no discrete GPU hardware, it optimizes dense multi-threaded throughput. Benchmark results demonstrate upper-tier performance in multi-core metrics, registering 85,051.53 on stress-ng, 39,975.0 on Clang software compilation, and 62.24 million Redis SET operations per second. In contrast, per-thread metrics such as Geekbench single-core (1,117.0) reflect entry-level performance. This tradeoff makes the instance an efficient platform for horizontally scalable, multi-threaded tasks including software build pipelines, web serving clusters, and caching layers.
